summary: Sawtooth throttling pattern during customer daily batch sweep causing intermittent 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ScoutMetrics runs a nightly daily-sweep job that uploads ~10k small embedding requests in bursts every 7 minutes between 02:00-04:00 UTC. Over the last three nights they saw a repeating sawtooth pattern of 429 responses — throughput spikes then a periodic waveform of throttles for ~30s, recovers briefly, then spikes again. This is affecting their pipelines (15-25% of batches failed), causing downstream retries and significant time-to-completion regression.

Impact:
- Approx 15-25% of batch embedding requests during sweep windows return 429s.
- Customer reports downstream job run time increase from ~12m to ~45m.
- Visible errors in their job logs; customer unable to complete daily indexing reliably.

Environment:
- Tenant: ScoutMetrics (dedicated pool, committed capacity).
- Region: prod-us-east (pool id: pool-ussc-07 provided by customer).
- API path: POST /v1/embeddings (batch upload via multipart clients).
- Keys: rotating short-lived keys used by their workers.

Observed behavior / logs provided by customer:
- 2026-03-09 02:07:13 UTC - burst of 10k requests, API returns 80% 200, 20% 429 distributed in ~30s window.
- Graph provided by customer: sawtooth pattern of error-rate with ~7m periodicity (attached as customer_graph_20260309.png).
- Customer log snippets: "ERROR: 429 rate limit - token_bucket_exhausted for tenant=ScoutMetrics pool=pool-ussc-07"

Steps to reproduce (customer job):
1) Start 200 concurrent worker processes each uploading 50 small documents in parallel to /v1/embeddings.
2) Repeat this at 7 minute cadence for a 2-hour window.
3) Observe intermittent 429s clustered as waveform spikes rather than uniform throttling.

Request from customer:
- Confirm why sawtooth throttle waveform occurs despite dedicated pool commitment.
- Provide recommended config changes (burst window, token refill, multiplexing guidance) and short-term mitigations to avoid daily job failures.
- Request SRE help to review pool telemetry (token-bucket accounting, health-check increments) and verify no cross-tenant bleed or health-checks causing miscounting.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ava Chen: Ticket opened after email from ScoutMetrics CS rep (case id SM-20260310-11). Attached customer graph and sample logs. Requesting initial triage.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Marco Silva: Assigned. Running initial checks: pulled tenant quotas and pool config for pool-ussc-07. No manual limit changes in last 30 days. Reproducing workload on staging to validate behavior.

2026-03-10 12:40 - Support (Marco Silva): Asked customer to provide exact timestamps, sample request IDs, and to confirm if workers use HTTP/2 multiplexing or short-lived API keys. Customer responded: multiplexing=enabled, keys=rotating every 10 minutes.

2026-03-11 02:45 - SRE (Leila Gomez): Observed periodic token-bucket depletion correlated with periodic warmup/scale events on the dedicated pool. Opening INT-5512 for investigation of autoscaler interactions. Linked thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C045POOL/p1678452000

2026-03-11 11:08 - Marco Silva: Performed controlled staging replay (200 workers * 50 docs) with multiplexing disabled: waveform suppressed, fewer 429s (suggests multiplexing interaction). Sharing logs and hypothesis to SRE.

2026-03-12 08:22 - Customer (ScoutMetrics rep - Jenna Patel): Verified that disabling per-worker HTTP/2 multiplexing reduced failures in their next sweep by ~70%. Requests guidance for configuration that preserves throughput but avoids throttles.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Marco Silva: Consolidating guidance and next steps; drafting recommended config changes (short term: staggered start, disable per-process multiplexing; medium term: increase pool burst allowance and adjust token refill smoothing).
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Token bucket accounting and refill interacts poorly with many short-lived multiplexed streams: multiplexed sessions may cause token consumption to appear burstier at the gateway, triggering rapid bucket depletion and a sawtooth recovery as refill kicks in.
- Autoscaler warmup/health-checks may briefly reduce usable capacity during scale events, amplifying transient throttle patterns in tight cadence jobs.
- Short-lived API key rotation every 10m may increase connection churn and transient per-key counters leading to uneven per-key accounting.

Telemetry reviewed:
- Pool metrics (pool-ussc-07): token_bucket_level graphs show sawtooth troughs synchronized with customer job cadence.
- Gateway logs: 429 reason strings show token_bucket_exhausted and occasionally health_check_increment.
- Autoscaler events: scale-up at 02:06 and 02:13 with 12-18s of instance churn visible in infra logs. Links: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/pool-ussc-07/token-buckets

Staging reproduction results:
- Full multiplexing enabled: reproduced waveform with 18% 429 rate.
- Multiplexing disabled (one connection per worker): waveform reduced, 4% 429 (mostly at peak saturations).
- Staggered worker-start with multiplexing enabled: waveform amplitude reduced significantly.
- Adjusted token refill smoothing on staging (simulated): smoother refill reduced peak 429s but increased tail latency slightly.

Actions taken:
- Requested SRE to whitelist short-term traffic exemption window for ScoutMetrics nightly sweep (pending approval via INT-5512).
- Requested autoscaler team to inspect warmup behavior for pool-ussc-07 (links to INT-5512).
- Drafted recommended client changes to customer: enable connection pooling at a worker-pool level instead of per-process multiplexing, add jitter to job start times, and increase per-request retry jitter/backoff to avoid synchronized retries.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 15:10 - Temporary mitigation: SRE applied temporary 15% burst allowance increase for pool-ussc-07 during 02:00-04:30 UTC sweep window. This reduced 429s to ~6% on next sweep (per customer report). See INT-5512 for audit trail.

Recommended long-term fixes provided to customer:
1) Client-side: change from per-process HTTP/2 multiplexing to a shared connection pool per worker-group, add randomized start jitter (0-90s) to sweep windows, and implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries.
2) Platform-side: modify token_bucket smoothing parameter for dedicated pools with high short-interval burst patterns; consider a dedicated burst credit for scheduled batch windows.
3) Ops: autoscaler warmup tuning for pool-ussc-07 to avoid transient capacity loss during recurring scale events.

Follow-ups / open work:
- INT-5512 assigned to autoscaler/SRE to root-cause warmup behavior and implement safe warmup adjustments (owner: Leila Gomez).
- Engineering ticket requested to evaluate gateway token accounting for multiplexed HTTP/2 sessions (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/412).
- Customer agreed to deploy client changes and share next run logs; Support will monitor two sweep windows then close the ticket if errors remain below 5%.
Status: Monitoring (Support will close after two successful sweep windows with <5% 429s).
